sections.value:
# PASS WITH NOTES — #271 round 2 of 2

Head: `8b08ba8f43726d7906076d4ef4fb2785f5472df9`.

**R271-001 is closed.** No remaining merge blocker. The two newly established limitations below are explicitly **C34 follow-ups**, not another review round.

## Fix verification

Reran the original A-build/check -> B-build -> A-install interleaving with two real Git worktrees, fake cargo, and the actual release-build/shared-build/installer scripts, all in a private temporary HOME, target and TMPDIR with spaces in their paths.

A's head was `f0bb909b6a`; B's was `e84c29962a`. After B built, the shared binary answered `(e84c29962a)`, while A successfully installed its private snapshot answering `(f0bb909b6a)`. Snapshot directories were mode 0700.

Independently delayed `--copy-out` using a FIFO: when cp opened the FIFO, the shared target lock still existed; after copying completed, shared-build exited and the lock was gone. This verifies the actual copy is inside the existing lock lifetime (`shared-build.sh:390-396`), not merely that the new option is present. An existing destination was refused with exit 6 and its bytes stayed unchanged.

The recipes install the returned snapshot and register EXIT cleanup. Native bounce cleans its returned snapshot after the install attempt, including the missing-HOME/error result path, before handling later daemon operations (`bounce/mod.rs:70-85`). Failed builds still propagate their status; stamp and install refusals remain before any signal to the old daemon. Later launch/health failures still have the explicitly documented pre-existing no-rollback behavior.

## C34 follow-up R271-002 — incomplete build-input closure

`release-build.sh:44-45` checks crates, manifests, Cargo config and the stamped extension trees, but omits production files embedded from outside those roots:

- Six hook/statusline scripts under `harness/scripts/`, embedded by `crates/harnesses/src/claude_settings.rs:28-38`.
- Five schemas under `.dd/schemas/pij/`, embedded by `crates/daemon/src/community/layout.rs:32-53`.
- Shipped `templates/roles/**/role.dd.json`, embedded by `crates/daemon/src/community/templates.rs:46-54`.

Individually dirtied representative files in each of those three roots in the fixture; the helper still exited 0 with the clean HEAD stamp. The fake build only establishes guard acceptance; the production include macros establish that these are real compile inputs. Extend the guard to that existing embed closure and cover representative changes. No repository-owned build.rs was found; migrations, crate manifests and the extra stamped control-commands fixture are already under crates. A dirty tracked crate source was correctly refused before a snapshot was left, and the intended local `.omp/models.yml` override was allowed.

## C34 follow-up R271-003 — interruption can leak a snapshot

`release-build.sh:59-77` has explicit error cleanup but no signal/EXIT cleanup while it owns the snapshot. Terminated only the temporary helper PID with SIGTERM after fake cargo started: helper exit -15, shared-build finished and released its lock, but one `pij-release.*` directory remained. A caller has not received its path yet, so caller-side cleanup cannot recover it.

The normal build-failure (101), stamp-failure (1), install-failure (1), and successful shell composition all left zero snapshots. Native cleanup also discards remove_dir_all errors (`bounce/mod.rs:83`), so cleanup is best effort rather than guaranteed. Follow up with ownership-aware signal cleanup and observable cleanup failures. The proof fixture removed its leaked directory during teardown; nothing was left in the machine's normal temp location.

## Evidence and cost

`just pr-freeze 271`: FINAL at the exact head; GitHub also reported successful TS checks, rust-lint and rust-test at this head.

`bash -n harness/scripts/release-build.sh harness/scripts/shared-build.sh`: passed.

Dependency-free Node execution of `recipeCostFindings` against the real justfile: passed, zero findings.

Local stdlib/fake-cargo proof: all 13 case assertions passed, including the original interleaving, lock-held copy, destination refusal, dirty-input probes, ordinary cleanup paths and the explicitly reproduced interruption limitation. No real cargo, deploy recipe, daemon operation, dependency installation or source modification.

No new steady-state loop, timer or per-seat work. One copy and bounded housekeeping per deploy; the existing shared-build contention polling remains per waiting build invocation. No live-fleet deployment measurement was performed by this reviewer.

**Harness gift:** the original interleaving is now encoded in the submitted tests. The remaining closure/cleanup regression opportunities are captured as `review-271-r2/SUGG-001`.
